context: Initially, root 1 (n1) has left child 2 (n2) and right leaf 3. Node 2 has left leaf 4 and right leaf 5. The node to insert, P, holds 0 and has no children. From left to right, the three panels show preparation for insertion, the completed insertion, and the completed removal.
description: The following steps trace the reference changes in the three panels above.
prose.result: Detaching P restores the original connections. We can conclude only that P is no longer reachable from the root. This neither establishes that its memory has been freed nor means that the whole left subtree was removed.

steps.announcement: The initial binary tree and the separate node P are ready for insertion.
steps.explanation: Before insertion, root 1 (n1) has left child 2 (n2) and right leaf 3. Node 2 has left leaf 4 and right leaf 5. Node P (value 0) is outside the tree with both children empty. Save a reference to node 2 in n2 before overwriting n1.left so that the entire original left subtree can be reattached.
steps.key_state: Before insertion, root 1 has left child 2 and right child 3, and 2 has left child 4 and right child 5. Node P (0) is still outside the tree.
steps.title: Prepare to insert P

steps.announcement: Assign two left pointers to insert P between nodes 1 and 2.
steps.explanation: Set n1.left = P and then P.left = n2. Root 1 now has left child P (0) and right leaf 3. P has left child 2 and no right child. Node 2 has left leaf 4 and right leaf 5. The reference saved in n2 reattaches node 2 with its entire subtree, preserving every original node.
steps.key_state: After insertion, root 1 has left child P (0) and right child 3. P has left child 2 and no right child. Node 2 has left child 4 and right child 5.
steps.title: Insert P into the left link

steps.announcement: Set n1.left = n2 to bypass P and restore the direct connection from the root to node 2.
steps.explanation: Set n1.left = n2 to bypass P and restore the original tree. Root 1 has left child 2 and right leaf 3. Node 2 has left leaf 4 and right leaf 5. P is now unreachable from the root, which does not imply that its memory has been freed.
steps.key_state: After detachment, root 1 has left child 2 and right child 3, and 2 has left child 4 and right child 5. P is unreachable from the root.
steps.title: Bypass P and reattach the original subtree

prose.summary: Redirect left child references to insert or detach an intermediate node P while keeping the entire subtree rooted at node 2.
prose.title: Inserting and detaching a node in a binary tree

context: Initially, root 1 (n1) has left child 2 (n2) and right leaf 3. Node 2 has left leaf 4 and right leaf 5. The node to insert, P, holds 0 and has no children. From left to right, the three panels show preparation for insertion, the completed insertion, and the completed removal.

frames.explanation: First save a reference to node 2 in n2. In the left panel, P is separate from the tree. In the middle panel, setting n1.left = P and P.left = n2 forms the left branch 1→P (0)→2. Node 2 keeps its children 4 and 5, and P has no right child. In the right panel, setting n1.left = n2 bypasses P and restores the original tree. Node 3 stays the right child of root 1 throughout.
